title: RGB MoCap Turns Your Video Into 3D Animation

viewer.who: 3D artists, animators and indie game devs
viewer.problem: Motion capture normally needs a tracking suit and a studio budget
viewer.job: Turn an ordinary video of a person into editable 3D character animation on a Windows PC

idea: Show RGB MoCap converting video to 3D motion using the project's official sample footage: source video, 3D reconstruction, skeleton and contact correction, character retargeting, and Blender export.

claims.text: RGB MoCap is a Windows application that converts a video of a person into editable 3D human animation, with AI models running locally.
It requires 64-bit Windows, a compatible NVIDIA GPU and OpenGL 4.3; it does not run on every PC and is not GPU-free.

Full-body models include ExMR, FlowHMR, GVHMR, MAMMA, PromptHMR and GEM-X; model files are downloaded separately in the Model Manager, some require registration or license acceptance, and all workflows together take about 77.8 GB.

Foot and hand contact timings can be corrected, motion can be retargeted onto 3D characters, and animation can be exported as FBX, BVH, VMD, a portable Blender project or UE5 FBX, with live bone streaming into Blender.

proof_plan.how_shown: Official project sample footage (docs/samples/motion-capture) shows the app reconstructing a dancer's motion in 3D beside the source video. The app could not be run on this Linux machine (Windows + NVIDIA GPU required), so no live capture is claimed; footage is the project's own published sample.
Payoff scene carries an on-screen 'WINDOWS · NVIDIA GPU · OPENGL 4.3' tag; the video never claims it works on every PC or without a GPU.
Model chips on screen (ExMR, FlowHMR, GVHMR, + MAMMA · PromptHMR · GEM-X) with fine print 'MODELS DOWNLOADED SEPARATELY — SOME NEED REGISTRATION' in the payoff scene.

Official samples show the skeleton/body inspect view with the contact-lock timeline, retargeted anime characters (character-retargeting sample), and the Blender Live Retarget view with bone mapping (streaming-to-blender sample); export chips list FBX, BVH, VMD, Blender project and UE5 FBX.

review.notes: Owner watched the finished Short and approved it ('rest is Good') after requesting removal of the scene kicker labels and the on-screen sample disclaimer; both were removed and the exact revised file was re-rendered, re-verified (full decode, loudness, contact sheet) and is the file pinned here. Footage remains the project's official samples; no live run is claimed. Owner requested Buffer + YouTube scheduling for tomorrow 6:15 PM New York.

Imagine turning an ordinary video into 3D character animation. RGB MoCap reconstructs a person's motion in 3D, lets you inspect the skeleton, correct foot and hand contacts, retarget the movement onto a 3D character, and export it for tools like Blender.

Requirements: 64-bit Windows, a compatible NVIDIA GPU and OpenGL 4.3. AI models (ExMR, FlowHMR, GVHMR, MAMMA, PromptHMR, GEM-X) are downloaded separately; some need registration. Footage: the project's official sample videos. AI-generated narration.
